name: LONGi Hi-MO2 bifacial PERC solar module
description: LONGi adapted monocrystalline PERC cells for a commercial module with a glass rear surface that could admit light. Its Hi-MO2 module reached mass production in 2017 and entered utility service at Southern Oak in Georgia, United States, in 2020.

places.note: Shanghai was the site of the public exhibition launch.
Southern Oak Solar Energy Center, Mitchell County, Georgia.

date.label: 19 April 2017
date.basis: LONGi gives the date and exhibition of the public unveiling.

events.statement: LONGi unveiled Hi-MO2 at the SNEC photovoltaic exhibition in Shanghai.
events.place_note: Shanghai, China, was the launch location.
events.scope: Public unveiling of the 60-cell and 72-cell Hi-MO2 module family.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph and Hi-MO2 product and production paragraphs
evidence.supports: Locates the April 19 unveiling at SNEC in Shanghai and identifies the bifacial PERC cells, glass rear package and Hi-MO1 antecedent.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs on Shanghai launch and Hi-MO1 technology platform
evidence.supports: Identifies higher-efficiency demand and China’s Top Runner programs as markets targeted by LONGi at launch.

date.label: By 24 April 2017
date.basis: The manufacturer reported mass production as already achieved.

events.statement: LONGi reported mass production of its 365 W Hi-MO2 module.
events.caveats: The announcement leaves the production start, factory location and production volume unresolved.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph and Hi-MO2 product and production paragraphs
evidence.supports: Reports the 365 W Hi-MO2 variant in mass production by 24 April.

date.label: First quarter of 2020
date.basis: Invenergy places the commercial start within the first quarter of 2020.

events.statement: Invenergy entered commercial operation at the Southern Oak Solar Energy Center with LONGi Hi-MO2 bifacial PERC modules paired with single-axis trackers and a power-purchase agreement with Georgia Power.
events.scope: Use of the Hi-MO2 product in a named utility-scale project.
events.caveats: The December 2019 date in the project filing refers to construction completion.

evidence.supports: Dates Southern Oak commissioning to the first quarter of 2020.

evidence.locator: pp. 29–30, Southern Oak case study and Solar Project Portfolio
evidence.supports: Identifies the deployed LONGi Hi-MO2 modules, 2020 commercial-operation year and 30-year Georgia Power contract.

evidence.locator: REDI awards, paragraph on the Invenergy subsidiary
evidence.supports: Names the 160 MW Invenergy project in Camilla and the Camilla Solar Energy LLC counterparty under the same REDI procurement.

earliest_record.rationale: The Shanghai unveiling is the earliest calendar-dated event entered here. The statement on mass production supplies an upper bound.

why: LONGi identified demand for more efficient products and China’s Top Runner programs as target markets. At Southern Oak, a successful bid under Georgia Power’s Renewable Energy Development Initiative secured a 30-year power-purchase agreement.

links.statement: LONGi’s bifacial monocrystalline design adapted the PERC architecture introduced at UNSW so the rear could collect light in a glass–glass module.
links.scope: Industrial use and modification of the rear-passivated cell design at the architecture level. The route by which LONGi acquired specific manufacturing know-how remains unresolved.
